Issue Details
### Background and motivation Running the same operation in-terms of different vector components is a fairly common operation. In order to make this easier, having indexers into the ``System.Numerics`` Vectors that returns the value at a position in the vector would make a ton of sense. Example:``v.X == v[0]``, ``v.Y == v[1]``, etc would ### API Proposal ```C# namespace System.Collections.Generic { public struct Vector3 : System.IEquatable, System.IFormattable { /// 0 is X, 1 is Y, 2 is Z public float this[int i] { get; } } } ``` ### API Usage ```C# Vector3 v3 = Vector3.UnitY; v3[0] == 0; v3[1] == 1; v3[2] == 0; ``` ### Risks None I don't think
Author: Avid29
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Numerics`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

@hypeartist I thought about it a little more, and now I do use that. 

However, I still believe this is a reasonable addition to the API. It's a sensible interpretation of the indexer on a Vector and Unity's Vectors already have this behavior.

review_comments: Same comment about `tab` leading to inconsistent indentation.
`Vector128<long>` has a `Count` of `2`, while you are processing all indices here in your `Assert.All`, so the 3rd+ entry is causing an exception
Similar issue exists for `Vector128Int32IndexerTest` and the `Vector64*IndexerTest`

This should likely goto two internal static helper methods `GetElement` and `WithElement` (where set is `this = WithElement(this, value)`) and where `Get/WithElement` match what `Vector128<float>` does for the same methods.

This will make it the easiest for me to add in the JIT intrinsification support in a follow up PR so this can be a single `extractps` and `insertps` instruction
`Vector4` has no helper methods like `GetElement` and `SetElement`

I was saying they should be added here and setup in a similar method to those that exist on `Vector64/128/256`.

`this[int index]` is an instance method and so the signature is internally something like `float get_Item(ref Vector4 self, int index)`. This makes it slightly more difficult to optimize/handle in the JIT and would require more significant work on my end later.

While if you set it up to call internal `static float GetElement(Vector4 vector, int index)` and `static Vector4 WithElement(Vector4 vector, int index, float value)` methods; then I can instead rely on all the existing JIT logic to accelerate these APIs, making my job much simpler.
Made a few more changes. Does this correspond to your ideas?
Nit: Is `this.` necessary here? The repo coding style is to avoid `this.` unless is is absolutely necessary (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/coding-guidelines/coding-style.md)

This one should become a `static method` in which case it would be `=> GetElement(this, index)`.

I explained why here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/60517#discussion_r730447156
(which basically sums up as, easier to share existing handling and avoids some issues with `this` being an implicit byref)
